items.followUp: Define the World Wide Web and state one use of it.

rubric.why: Shows what the Internet is.
rubric.description: Defines the Internet as a worldwide network of interconnected computers or networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a worldwide network connecting computers or networks.

rubric.why: Shows the purpose of the Internet.
rubric.description: States that it enables communication or sharing information and resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid purpose.

modelAnswer: The Internet is a worldwide network of interconnected computer networks.
It allows people to communicate and share information and resources.

items.followUp: Write two examples of private IPv4 addresses.

rubric.description: Gives one valid IPv4 address in dotted-decimal form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid example.

rubric.why: The question asks for two examples.
rubric.description: Gives a second valid IPv4 address, distinct from the first.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second valid example.

items.followUp: What is a communication medium? Give one example.

rubric.why: Identifies the channel as the means or medium of transmission.
rubric.description: Defines a communication channel as the medium or path through which data travels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the medium or path for data transmission.

rubric.why: Identifies communication between its endpoints.
rubric.description: States that the channel carries data from a sender to a receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the data's source and destination.

modelAnswer: A communication channel is the medium or path through which data is transmitted.
It carries data from a sender to a receiver.

items.followUp: Write HTML code to create a hyperlink to example.com with the text “Visit”.

rubric.why: Identifies the anchor tag and its link attribute.
rubric.description: Uses an anchor tag with the href attribute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly using an anchor and href.

rubric.why: Shows the link text enclosed by the anchor element.
rubric.description: Includes link text between the opening and closing anchor tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including link text and a closing anchor tag.

items.followUp: What is a web browser? Name one web browser.

rubric.why: Identifies the browser's role in accessing web pages.
rubric.description: States that a browser is used to access or retrieve web pages.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct access or retrieval purpose.

rubric.why: Identifies how a browser presents web content to users.
rubric.description: States that a browser displays web pages for the user.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it displays or renders web pages.

modelAnswer: A web browser is used to access and retrieve web pages from the Internet.
It displays the pages so that users can view and interact with them.

rubric.description: Identifies a tag as markup, such as an opening or closing tag.

rubric.why: Shows that an element includes more than just its tags.
rubric.description: Explains that an element consists of its tag or tags together with its content.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for distinguishing the element as including content and tags.

modelAnswer:
An HTML tag is markup written inside angle brackets, such as

or

items.followUp: What is test data? Give one example of normal test data and explain why it is used.

rubric.why: Defines test data by its role in testing a program.
rubric.description: Defines test data as input values used to test a program.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that test data is input used during testing.

rubric.why: Explains a key purpose of testing.
rubric.description: States that testing helps find errors or check whether the program produces expected results.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid testing purpose.

rubric.why: Provides a concrete example of test data.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of test input, such as entering 75 as a student's marks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant, specific test-data example.

rubric.why: Connects the example input to checking program behaviour.
rubric.description: Explains that the program's output for the example is checked against the expected result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the expected output or checking the result.

modelAnswer: Test data is the input data given to a program to test whether it works correctly.
Testing is important because it helps find errors and checks that the program produces the expected results.
For example, enter 75 as a student's marks in a grading program.
Check that the program displays the expected grade for 75 marks.

items.followUp: Define the TCP/IP protocol suite and explain the role of the IP protocol.

rubric.why: Defines TCP/IP as a group of communication rules or protocols.
rubric.description: Defines the TCP/IP protocol suite as a set of protocols used for communication over networks or the Internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a protocol suite for network communication.

rubric.why: Identifies a valid protocol and its function.
rubric.description: Explains that TCP breaks data into packets and/or helps ensure reliable delivery.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct TCP role.

rubric.why: Identifies the other protocol and its function.
rubric.description: Explains that IP uses addresses and/or routes packets to their destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct IP role.

rubric.why: Shows how the protocols support data transfer across networks.
rubric.description: States that TCP/IP enables data to travel between devices over interconnected networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining its role in transferring data between networked devices.

modelAnswer: The TCP/IP protocol suite is a set of rules and protocols that enables communication between devices over networks, including the Internet.
TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) breaks data into packets and helps ensure that they are delivered reliably and in the correct order.
IP (Internet Protocol) provides addressing and routes packets to their destination across networks.
Together, TCP and IP enable data to be transferred between devices.
